metadata.title: nab-Paclitaxel Monotherapy - 21 day
metadata.indication: Metastatic breast cancer in adults after failure of first-line metastatic therapy when standard anthracycline-containing therapy is not indicated.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Source reconciled · independent clinical/pharmacy review pending

metadata.catalogue_source_check_scope: Catalogue presence and source link structure only; not rule level source fidelity.
metadata.schedule_summary: Nab-paclitaxel on Day 1 every 21 days. Review response after two cycles; the NCCP protocol says to discontinue if there is no response. Further treatment depends on benefit and tolerance.
audited_eligibility: Metastatic breast cancer in adults after failure of first-line metastatic therapy when standard anthracycline-containing therapy is not indicated.
No hypersensitivity to nab-paclitaxel, albumin or excipients
Grade ≥2 neuropathy is a caution, not a blanket exclusion
audit_limitations: Independent clinical and oncology-pharmacy review remains pending; source reconciliation is not clinical-use authorisation.
No fixed routine CT, tumour-marker or cardiac-monitoring interval is specified; use the individual treatment plan.
Dose history is required before a numeric reduction; existing reductions must not be re-escalated.
Table 1 intermediate count row prints 220 mg without /m²; retain the unit discrepancy for pharmacy review instead of silently correcting it.

baseline: Cardiac assessment if significant cardiac history or previous anthracycline exposure
ongoing: FBC, renal and liver profile before every cycle
Assess treatment response, including the source review after 2 cycles
source_monitoring.imaging: History/exposure-triggered baseline assessment, then clinical indication; no fixed HER2-style echo schedule.

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: Any dose modification should be discussed with a Consultant.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding of the current NCCP source. It does not replace the NCCP regimen, clinical judgement, local policy, prescribing review or pharmacy verification.

supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for low emetogenic risk
supportive_care.mapping_basis: Use the highest-risk active component and the current source-specific support plan.
supportive_care.premedication: None usually required for nab-paclitaxel; do not copy the routine solvent-based paclitaxel allergy-premedication schedule.

indications.description: Metastatic breast cancer in adults after failure of first-line metastatic therapy when standard anthracycline-containing therapy is not indicated.

eligibility: Metastatic breast cancer in adults after failure of first-line metastatic therapy when standard anthracycline-containing therapy is not indicated.
No hypersensitivity to nab-paclitaxel, albumin or excipients
Grade ≥2 neuropathy is a caution, not a blanket exclusion

baseline: Cardiac assessment such as ECG and ECHO/MUGA if significant cardiac history or prior anthracyclines
regular: FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle
Cardiac function only when clinically indicated

treatment_phases.name: Nab-paclitaxel every 3 weeks
treatment_phases.label: Nab-paclitaxel every 3 weeks

administration.notes: Over 30 minutes; use 15 μm filter. Not interchangeable with other paclitaxel formulations.

treatment_phases.duration_text: Nab-paclitaxel 260 mg/m² IV over 30 minutes on Day 1 every 21 days. Assess response after two cycles; discontinue if there is no response. Otherwise continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
